name: Cannoli Siciliani
description: Mahogany-brown fried pastry tubes — crisp enough to shatter at the first bite — filled to order with a sweetened ricotta cream fragrant with orange zest and studded with mini chocolate chips, the filling cool and dense against the hot crunch of the shell.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Candied orange peel or toasted seeds (ends); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one

name: Cannoli Siciliani (gluten-free)
description: Mahogany-brown fried pastry tubes — crisp enough to shatter at the first bite — filled to order with a sweetened ricotta cream fragrant with orange zest and studded with mini chocolate chips, the filling cool and dense against the hot crunch of the shell. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Candied orange peel or toasted seeds (ends); the source also suggests a nut option; use the first one

name: Caponata
description: The agrodolce soul of a Sicilian summer — eggplant fried to a meaty collapse, folded into a glossy tangle of celery, capers, and olives, then braised in tomato and lacquered with a sweet-sour vinegar glaze that deepens for a day before it ever reaches the table.

ingredients.note: Toasted pine nuts and torn basil

name: Caponata (nut-free)
description: The agrodolce soul of a Sicilian summer — eggplant fried to a meaty collapse, folded into a glossy tangle of celery, capers, and olives, then braised in tomato and lacquered with a sweet-sour vinegar glaze that deepens for a day before it ever reaches the table. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: instead of Toasted pine nuts and torn basil

name: Pasta Carbonara
description: Rome's greatest sleight of hand — guanciale crisped in its own fat, egg yolks and Pecorino Romano tempered off the heat with starchy pasta water until the pasta is lacquered in a glossy, cream-free sauce that clings to every strand. No cream, no butter. Technique alone makes the silk.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek, cut into lardons or batons)
Pecorino Romano (very finely grated, almost powdery)
Pasta cooking water (heavily salted, starchy — reserved just before draining)

name: Pasta Carbonara (gluten-free)
description: Rome's greatest sleight of hand — guanciale crisped in its own fat, egg yolks and Pecorino Romano tempered off the heat with starchy pasta water until the pasta is lacquered in a glossy, cream-free sauce that clings to every strand. No cream, no butter. Technique alone makes the silk. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free pasta shapes instead of dried pasta.

ingredients.note: Guanciale (cured pork cheek, cut into lardons or batons)
Pecorino Romano (very finely grated, almost powdery)
Pasta cooking water (heavily salted, starchy — reserved just before draining)

name: Carnitas
description: Michoacán's gift to the taco: pork shoulder braised slow in its own rendered fat with orange, bay, and a whisper of cinnamon, then fried in that same fat until the edges shatter and the center stays meltingly tender. Crispy outside, juicy inside — the eternal carnitas contradiction.

name: Carottes Vichy (Glazed Carrots)
description: Carrots simmered in Vichy water, butter, and a whisper of sugar until tender and lacquered — a humble side that shines with sweetness and shine.

name: Cassoulet
description: A deep terrine of creamy Tarbais beans buried under duck confit and Toulouse sausage, baked until a golden, crunchy bread-crumb crust forms and reforms three times over — the soul of Languedoc in a single pot.

ingredients.note: Dried Tarbais beans (or flageolet, soaked overnight)
Duck confit legs (2 legs, from confit-duck-legs)
Chicken or pork stock; made up to 1000 ml with boiling water
Day-old white bread (blitzed into coarse crumbs)

name: Cassoulet (gluten-free)
description: A deep terrine of creamy Tarbais beans buried under duck confit and Toulouse sausage, baked until a golden, crunchy gluten-free bread-crumb crust forms and reforms three times over — the soul of Languedoc in a single pot. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: Dried Tarbais beans (or flageolet, soaked overnight)
Duck confit legs (2 legs, from confit-duck-legs)
Chicken or pork stock; made up to 1000 ml with boiling water
instead of Day-old white bread (blitzed into coarse crumbs)

name: Cauliflower Shawarma
description: A whole cauliflower head lacquered in warm spices and roasted until the florets caramelise to a crackling amber — crunchy where exposed, yielding and smoky at the core.

ingredients.note: Shawarma spice blend (cumin, coriander, turmeric, smoked paprika, cinnamon, allspice)

name: Ceviche Clásico
description: Peru's national dish in its purest form: raw sea bass cut into even cubes and immersed in a fierce tide of fresh lime juice, ají amarillo, and ginger, the acid transforming the fish into something simultaneously cooked and alive — bright, quivering, burning, and cold. The leche de tigre left in the bowl afterwards is worth drinking.

ingredients.note: Sushi-grade sea bass (corvina or lenguado), cut into 2 cm cubes
Cancha (toasted Peruvian corn) or chifles (fried plantain chips)
Ají limo or habanero, seeded and very finely minced

name: Ceviche de Camarones
description: Unlike fish ceviche, shrimp ceviche begins with a brief poach — the gentle heat setting the protein just enough to give the shrimp their characteristic snap before the lime and ají amarillo take over and brighten every edge. The leche de tigre that accumulates at the bottom of the bowl is so vibrantly good it is traditionally drunk straight from the glass.

ingredients.note: Large shrimp (21–25 count), peeled and deveined

name: Chana Masala
description: Chickpeas braised into a deep, rust-red onion-tomato masala built on a layered spice technique — whole spices bloomed in hot oil, ground spices toasted into the gravy, and a final lift of tart amchoor that makes the whole pot ring.

ingredients.note: Whole spices (2 black cardamom, 1 cinnamon shard, 2 cloves, 1 tsp cumin seed, 2 bay leaves)
Ground spice blend (1 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp Kashmiri chile, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp garam masala)

name: Char Siu (Cantonese BBQ Pork)
description: Strips of pork shoulder disappear into an overnight bath of honey, hoisin, and fermented red bean curd before emerging from a hot oven with a crackling lacquer glaze that shatters faintly under the knife, revealing a blush-pink interior that is simultaneously sweet, funky, and smoky. The char at the edges — where the honey catches and darkens — is the flavor the entire dish is built around.

ingredients.note: Pork shoulder or pork neck (with some fat marbling)
Fermented red bean curd (nan ru), mashed smooth

name: Chard with Currants and Pine Nuts
description: Wilted rainbow chard braised with golden raisins and pine nuts in olive oil — the sweet-and-savory Sicilian agrodolce that turns a humble green into something worth seeking out.

ingredients.note: Rainbow chard, stems separated and sliced into 2 cm pieces, leaves roughly torn

name: Chard with Currants and Sunflower seeds (nut-free)
description: Wilted rainbow chard braised with golden raisins and sunflower seeds in olive oil — the sweet-and-savory Sicilian agrodolce that turns a humble green into something worth seeking out. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts.

ingredients.note: Rainbow chard, stems separated and sliced into 2 cm pieces, leaves roughly torn

name: Chicken Katsu
description: Chicken thighs pounded to an even thickness, coated in panko breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried until deep golden — shatteringly crisp exterior, moist interior — served with tonkatsu sauce.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for shallow frying (rice bran or canola); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Chicken Katsu (gluten-free)
description: Chicken thighs pounded to an even thickness, coated in gluten-free breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried until deep golden — shatteringly crisp exterior, moist interior — served with tonkatsu sauce. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour, gluten-free breadcrumbs instead of breadcrumbs, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of worcestershire sauce, oyster sauce (gluten-free) instead of oyster sauce.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for shallow frying (rice bran or canola); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Chicken Marsala
description: Pounded chicken cutlets seared in a ripping hot pan, then swathed in a sauce of Marsala wine and earthy cremini mushrooms that reduces to a deep amber lacquer. The wine's caramel-oxidized sweetness plays against the savory fond in a way that makes a thirty-minute dinner taste like it spent the afternoon on the stove.

ingredients.note: Chicken stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Chicken Marsala (gluten-free)
description: Pounded chicken cutlets seared in a ripping hot pan, then swathed in a sauce of Marsala wine and earthy cremini mushrooms that reduces to a deep amber lacquer. The wine's caramel-oxidized sweetness plays against the savory fond in a way that makes a thirty-minute dinner taste like it spent the afternoon on the stove. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Chicken stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Pollo en Mole Poblano
description: Chicken thighs simmered in the great mole of Puebla — a baroque sauce of four dried chiles, charred bread, dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds and a dozen spices, its depth coming from layers of charred, fried and ground ingredients folded one atop another. Complex without being complicated: every step has a purpose.

ingredients.note: Chipotle chiles in adobo (or 2 dried morita chiles)
Stale white bread slice, fried in lard until golden
Ripe roma tomatoes (charred whole under broiler until blackened)
White onion half (charred cut-side down in a dry skillet)
Garlic cloves (charred unpeeled in a dry skillet, then peeled)
Chicken stock (warm); made up to 1000 ml with boiling water

name: Pollo en Mole Poblano (gluten-free)
description: Chicken thighs simmered in the great mole of Puebla — a baroque sauce of four dried chiles, charred gluten-free bread, dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds and a dozen spices, its depth coming from layers of charred, fried and ground ingredients folded one atop another. Complex without being complicated: every step has a purpose. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread.

ingredients.note: Chipotle chiles in adobo (or 2 dried morita chiles)
instead of Stale white bread slice, fried in lard until golden
Ripe roma tomatoes (charred whole under broiler until blackened)

name: Pollo en Mole Negro
description: Bone-in chicken pieces simmered low and slow in mole negro until the dark, bittersweet sauce coats every surface and the meat pulls from the bone in silken threads — the defining celebration dish of Oaxaca, where complexity is measured in chiles and time.

ingredients.note: Bone-in chicken pieces (legs, thighs, and drumsticks)
Mole negro paste (Oaxacan or commercial, e.g. Doña Maria)
Chicken stock, warm; made up to 750 ml with boiling water

name: Chicken Piccata
description: Thin pounded cutlets seared to a gold that borders on bronze, then drowned in a pan sauce sharp with lemon and briny with capers. The butter mounts at the last second, turning an acidic reduction into something glossy and round.

ingredients.note: Chicken stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Chicken Piccata (gluten-free)

The butter mounts at the last second, turning an acidic reduction into something glossy and round. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Chicken stock; made up to 50 ml with boiling water

name: Austrian Chicken Schnitzel
description: A chicken breast pounded to translucency, dressed in fine breadcrumbs, and shallow-fried in clarified butter until the coating billows away from the meat like a souffleed golden shell — the quintessential Vienna technique applied to poultry.

ingredients.note: Fine sea salt and white pepper

name: Austrian Chicken Schnitzel (gluten-free)

ingredients.note: instead of Fine dried breadcrumbs (not panko)
Fine sea salt and white pepper

name: Chicken Shawarma
description: Spiced, herb-scented chicken thighs slowly roasted until their edges catch and char, then sliced thin for wraps — warm spice, caramelized crust, juicy interior.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Charred yogurt-marinated chicken folded into a velvety, fenugreek-scented tomato gravy enriched with cream — smoky at the edges, warm and rounded at the core. The dish that bridges a Punjabi tandoor and a British curry house.

ingredients.note: Boneless chicken thigh (cut into 4 cm pieces)
Kashmiri red chili powder (deep red, mild)

name: Chicken Tortilla Soup
description: A brick-red, gently smoky tomato-and-chile broth full of shredded chicken thigh, sweet corn, and black beans, finished with a squeeze of lime and a crackling tangle of oven-crisped corn tortilla strips that soften at the edges as you eat.

ingredients.note: Chipotle chiles in adobo, minced with their sauce
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 1500 ml with boiling water
Corn kernels, frozen or cut from the cob
Cilantro, avocado (diced), and crumbled queso fresco

name: Chickpea Spinach Coconut Curry
description: Tender chickpeas simmered in a velvety tomato-coconut gravy warm with cumin, ginger, and turmeric, with handfuls of spinach wilted in at the end. Mellow and creamy, brightened with a squeeze of lime.

name: Picadillo Filling for Chiles en Nogada
description: A baroque and beautiful minced pork picadillo woven through with sweet dried fruit, warm spices, and the haunting brightness of fresh peach and pear — the stuffing for Mexico's most celebrated seasonal dish, a recipe that carries August in every bite.

ingredients.note: Fresh peach or pear, peeled and finely diced

name: Picadillo Filling for Chiles en Nogada (nut-free)
description: A baroque and beautiful minced pork picadillo woven through with sweet dried fruit, warm spices, and the haunting brightness of fresh peach and pear — the stuffing for Mexico's most celebrated seasonal dish, a recipe that carries August in every bite. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

ingredients.note: instead of Blanched almonds, roughly chopped
Fresh peach or pear, peeled and finely diced

name: Cantonese Garlic-Braised Eggplant
description: Eggplant pieces flash-fried until their centres are silky and their skins go glossy, then braised in a glossy, deeply savoury garlic sauce that clings to each piece like lacquer — the kind of dish that makes plain white rice disappear.

ingredients.note: Chinese or Japanese eggplant, cut into 5 cm batons
Neutral oil for frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)
Vegetable stock or water; made up to 100 ml with boiling water
Dried chilli flakes and white pepper

name: Cantonese Garlic-Braised Eggplant (gluten-free)

name: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard
description: Zhēng dàn — a savory custard so silky it trembles at the touch of a spoon, its surface smooth as polished jade, topped with a few drops of soy and sesame oil that pool into dark, fragrant islands.

ingredients.note: Spring onion, finely sliced on the bias

name: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard (gluten-free)

ingredients.note: instead of Light soy sauce (for custard)

name: Chocolate Fondant (Molten Lava Cake)
description: A deeply dark individual chocolate cake with a barely-set shell that collapses on the plate to release a river of liquid ganache from the centre — the margin between triumph and disaster is exactly two minutes in the oven.

name: Dark Chocolate Ganache
description: Cream and chocolate collapse into each other in a glossy, jet-black emulsion that clings to a spoon like liquid velvet. At room temperature it pours like a mirror glaze; chilled, it sets to a truffle-firm fudge you can slice clean.

ingredients.note: Light corn syrup (for gloss and shelf life)

name: Chocolate Lava Cake
description: A paradox in a ramekin — a cake with a fully set chocolate shell that conceals a dark, flowing center of pure molten ganache, the interior flowing out in a slow, warm river when the spoon breaks through the thin crust.

name: Chocolate Lava Cake (gluten-free)
description: A paradox in a ramekin — a cake with a fully set chocolate shell that conceals a dark, flowing center of pure molten ganache, the interior flowing out in a slow, warm river when the spoon breaks through the thin crust. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Chocolate Mousse
description: The classic mousse au chocolat — bittersweet chocolate enriched with egg yolks, then lifted by a glossy meringue and softly whipped cream into a cloud that holds a swooped peak yet dissolves the instant it touches the tongue. Dark, deep, and barely sweet.

name: Choucroute Garnie
description: Alsatian braised sauerkraut — rinsed to tame its sharpness, then slow-cooked in Riesling with juniper and bay until silk-tender, piled high with smoked pork knuckle, sausages, and lardons. A dish that makes winter honorable.

name: Churros con Chocolate
description: Crisp, ridged ropes of fried choux dough — golden and shattering at the ridges, yielding within — dusted in cinnamon sugar and plunged into a cup of velvet-thick, bittersweet Spanish hot chocolate.

name: Churros con Chocolate (gluten-free)
description: Crisp, ridged ropes of fried choux dough — golden and shattering at the ridges, yielding within — dusted in cinnamon sugar and plunged into a cup of velvet-thick, bittersweet Spanish hot chocolate. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Spanish Churros
description: Crisp-ridged, grease-free fried dough piped star-shaped and rolled in cinnamon sugar — the breakfast of Madrid, best plunged still hot into a cup of thick, almost-solid hot chocolate, the batter inside still just slightly damp at the centre.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Spanish Churros (gluten-free)
description: Crisp-ridged, grease-free fried dough piped star-shaped and rolled in cinnamon sugar — the breakfast of Madrid, best plunged still hot into a cup of thick, almost-solid hot chocolate, the batter inside still just slightly damp at the centre. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: Neutral oil for deep-frying; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder with Apples
description: Pork shoulder browned hard and braised low in dry cider with onions, carrots, and thyme until it slumps apart at a touch, finished with tart apple wedges and a mustard-sharpened, glossy sauce.

ingredients.note: Yellow onions, sliced into thick half-moons
Chicken stock, low-sodium; made up to 250 ml with boiling water
Firm, tart apples (such as Granny Smith), cored and cut into eighths

name: Cioppino
description: San Francisco's magnificent fish stew — Dungeness crab, clams, mussels, shrimp, and firm fish simmered in a spiced tomato-wine broth thick enough to coat bread, the Italian-American fisherman's answer to bouillabaisse.

ingredients.note: Dungeness crab, cracked into sections (or king crab legs)
Firm white fish (halibut or sea bass), 4 cm chunks
Canned whole San Marzano tomatoes, hand-crushed

name: Cioppino (gluten-free)

Firm white fish (halibut or sea bass), 4 cm chunks

name: Cherry Clafoutis
description: A loose, eggy batter poured over whole black cherries and baked until it puffs like a soufflé and settles to something between a thick crêpe and a soft pudding. The cherries weep their juice into the custard below, staining it a deep burgundy while the top turns golden and the kitchen fills with the smell of warm fruit and vanilla.

name: Cherry Clafoutis (gluten-free)
description: A loose, eggy batter poured over whole black cherries and baked until it puffs like a soufflé and settles to something between a thick crêpe and a soft pudding. The cherries weep their juice into the custard below, staining it a deep burgundy while the top turns golden and the kitchen fills with the smell of warm fruit and vanilla. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Clams Casino
description: Rhode Island's proudest bar snack: littleneck clams half-shelled and loaded with a smoky mix of bacon, sweet pepper, and butter, then broiled until the clam liquor bubbles and the bacon edges crisp to a dark, salty crunch.

name: Thai Coconut Ice Cream
description: No-churn coconut ice cream made with full-fat coconut cream and palm sugar, frozen without a machine into a dense, creamy mass that melts on the tongue in a wave of tropical fat — the palm sugar's caramel-molasses depth threading through the clean white coconut like a dark ribbon. Served in a small wafer cone or over sticky rice on the street, this is simplicity perfected.

ingredients.note: Palm sugar, grated or broken (not refined white)
Condensed coconut milk (or regular sweetened condensed milk)
Pandan leaf, tied in a knot (optional)

name: Coconut Prawn Curry
description: Tiger prawns simmered in a golden, fragrant coconut curry alive with lemongrass, galangal and fresh turmeric — fresh, quick and bracingly bright. The south of Thailand in a bowl: coconut-sweet, fish-sauce-salty, lime-sour, chili-warm.

ingredients.note: Tiger prawns, shell-on and heads on
Lemongrass stalks, outer layers removed, bruised
Palm sugar or soft brown sugar
Fresh red chilies, deseeded and sliced

name: Cold Sesame Noodles
description: Wheat noodles, cooked and cooled, tossed in a sauce of tahini and Chinese sesame paste, soy, black vinegar, chili oil, and a whisper of sugar — nutty, saline, sour, and hot all at once, a sauce so good you want to drink it. Cucumber julienne and scallion add crunch and green brightness against the yielding, slippery noodles.

ingredients.note: Fresh or dried Chinese wheat noodles (medium thickness)
Chinese sesame paste (zhima jiang) or tahini

name: Cold Sesame Noodles (gluten-free)
description: Rice noodles, cooked and cooled, tossed in a sauce of tahini and Chinese sesame paste, soy, black vinegar, chili oil, and a whisper of sugar — nutty, saline, sour, and hot all at once, a sauce so good you want to drink it. Cucumber julienne and scallion add crunch and green brightness against the yielding, slippery noodles. This gluten-free version uses rice noodles instead of egg noodles, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, rice vinegar instead of chinese black vinegar.

ingredients.note: instead of Fresh or dried Chinese wheat noodles (medium thickness)
Chinese sesame paste (zhima jiang) or tahini
instead of Chinkiang black rice vinegar

name: Creamy Coleslaw
description: Shredded cabbage tossed in a tangy, slightly sweet mayonnaise dressing that has had an hour to draw out the cabbage's moisture and concentrate it into a crisp, glossy, deeply flavored slaw — the definitive BBQ side dish.

ingredients.note: Green cabbage, cored and finely shredded
Celery seed, kosher salt, black pepper

name: Confit de Canard
description: Duck legs cured overnight in salt, then submerged in their own rendered fat and cooked at a barely trembling temperature until the collagen dissolves and the meat is silky and almost boneless. Crisped in a screaming-hot pan before serving, the skin shatters.

ingredients.note: Duck fat; for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Confit Garlic
description: Whole garlic cloves poached with the patience of a slow afternoon in extra-virgin olive oil at barely 90°C — the sharp, pungent allium slowly melting into something butter-soft, golden-tinged, honeyed and completely sweet. The oil becomes liquid gold. Both are a kitchen staple that transforms everything they touch.

ingredients.note: Extra-virgin olive oil (enough to submerge); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Congee
description: The quiet patience of rice surrendering to water — grains swelling, then bursting, then dissolving into a silken white porridge that carries the faint breath of ginger and tastes of comfort itself.

name: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
description: North Africa's communal centerpiece — semolina couscous steamed twice until each grain is featherlight and separate, served over a broth-rich stew of seven vegetables scented with ras el hanout and saffron, the whole table gathering around a single, fragrant mound.

ingredients.note: Savoy or green cabbage, cut in wedges

name: Quinoa with Seven Vegetables (gluten-free)

This gluten-free version uses quinoa instead of couscous.

ingredients.note: Savoy or green cabbage, cut in wedges

name: Maryland Crab Cakes
description: Chunky jumbo lump crab bound minimally with egg and Old Bay, formed into thick patties, and seared in butter until the exterior is golden and the interior stays barely bound — almost all crab, no filler.

ingredients.note: Jumbo lump blue crab meat (picked for shell)

ingredients.note: Jumbo lump blue crab meat (picked for shell)
instead of Fine breadcrumbs or crushed crackers

name: Creamy Lemon Chicken Pasta with Spinach
description: Short pasta and golden-seared chicken folded through a light cream and Parmesan sauce that stays bright with lemon zest and juice, with a big handful of spinach collapsing into ribbons at the last second.

ingredients.note: Short pasta (penne, fusilli or casarecce), dry
Kosher salt, for the pasta water
Kosher salt, for the chicken and sauce

name: Creamy Lemon Chicken Pasta with Spinach (gluten-free)

ingredients.note: instead of Short pasta (penne, fusilli or casarecce), dry
Kosher salt, for the pasta water

name: Crema Catalana
description: Catalonia's ancient answer to crème brûlée — a silky egg-yolk custard perfumed with lemon zest and cinnamon rather than vanilla, set in shallow terracotta dishes and finished with a brittle caramel crust burned with a red-hot iron.

ingredients.note: Caster sugar (plus extra for the crust)
Lemon zest (1 large lemon, no pith)

name: Creme Caramel
description: A trembling dome of vanilla custard floating on a mirror of bitter caramel — the most elegant dessert that asks nothing of the cook but patience and a gentle hand.

name: Crème Pâtissière (Pastry Cream)
description: The workhorse of the French gluten-free pastry kitchen — a thick, deeply vanilla-scented cream that sets firm enough to pipe into éclairs or crown a tart, yet dissolves on the tongue into pure silk and warmth.

ingredients.note: Vanilla bean, split and scraped (or 2 tsp extract)

name: Crêpes Suzette
description: The grand finale of the old French dining room — gossamer-thin crêpes folded into quarters and bathed in a glossy beurre Suzette of caramelized sugar, fresh orange juice and butter, then set alight tableside with a hiss of Grand Marnier until the flames die to a lacquer of warm citrus and toffee.

name: Crêpes Suzette (gluten-free)

This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

name: Slow-Rendered Crispy Duck Legs
description: Duck legs cured overnight with thyme and salt, then rendered low and slow until the fat is completely liquid beneath a skin that shatters on first bite — the Gascon tradition of patience turning one of the richest cuts in the kitchen into something impossibly light and crisp.

name: Crispy Pork Belly
description: Cantonese siu yuk at its finest — the skin shatters into a thousand lacquered shards, the fat beneath has rendered to a translucent, yielding layer, and the meat below is seasoned deep into the grain.

name: Crispy Tofu Lettuce Cups
description: Crumbled tofu fried until browned and crackly, tossed with minced shiitake, crunchy water chestnuts, and a sticky ginger-hoisin glaze, then spooned into cold, crisp butter lettuce leaves. Hot and cold, savory and fresh in one bite.

ingredients.note: Scallions, whites and greens separated, sliced
Butter lettuce, leaves separated and chilled

name: Crispy Tofu Lettuce Cups (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Crumbled tofu fried until browned and crackly, tossed with minced shiitake, crunchy water chestnuts, and a sticky ginger-gluten-free hoisin glaze, then spooned into cold, crisp butter lettuce leaves. Hot and cold, savory and fresh in one bite. This gluten- & nut-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, hoisin sauce (gluten-free) instead of hoisin sauce, sunflower seeds instead of cashew nuts.

ingredients.note: Scallions, whites and greens separated, sliced
Butter lettuce, leaves separated and chilled

name: Crispy Tofu Peanut Noodles
description: Chewy wheat noodles slicked in a glossy, gingery peanut-lime sauce, piled with shatter-edged cubes of golden tofu and cool ribbons of cucumber. Nutty, salty, a little sweet, with a slow chili-crisp warmth underneath.

ingredients.note: Extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes

name: Crispy Tofu Sunflower seed Noodles (gluten- & nut-free)
description: Chewy rice noodles slicked in a glossy, gingery sunflower seed-lime sauce, piled with shatter-edged cubes of golden tofu and cool ribbons of cucumber. Nutty, salty, a little sweet, with a slow chili-crisp warmth underneath. This gluten- & nut-free version uses rice noodles instead of egg noodles, sunflower seed butter instead of peanut butter, tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce, sunflower seeds instead of peanuts.

ingredients.note: Extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes
instead of Dried wheat noodles (egg-free), medium thickness
instead of Roasted peanuts, roughly chopped

name: Croque-Monsieur
description: The Parisian café sandwich elevated by proper béchamel — buttery bread, good ham, nutmeg-scented white sauce, and Gruyère that bubbles and blisters under the broiler into a savoury, slightly charred crust that crackles when you press down on it.

ingredients.note: Thick-cut white bread (pain de mie preferred)
Gruyère, coarsely grated (Comté or Emmental work too)

name: Croque-Monsieur (gluten-free)
description: The Parisian café sandwich elevated by proper béchamel — buttery gluten-free bread, good ham, nutmeg-scented white sauce, and Gruyère that bubbles and blisters under the broiler into a savoury, slightly charred crust that crackles when you press down on it. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free bread instead of crusty white bread, gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: instead of Thick-cut white bread (pain de mie preferred)
Gruyère, coarsely grated (Comté or Emmental work too)

name: Cuban Black Beans (Frijoles Negros)
description: A sofrito of onion, green pepper, and garlic cooked down to a rich, sweet base carries black beans through a long simmer until the liquid becomes thick and dark as ink — seasoned with cumin and a splash of vinegar added at the very end, the brightness cuts through the deep, earthy richness like a sharp note on a low chord.

ingredients.note: Dried black beans (soaked overnight, or canned)
Apple cider vinegar or dry white wine

name: Curried Carrot & Red Lentil Soup
description: Sweet carrots and red lentils collapse into a velvety, sunset-orange purée warmed with ginger and curry spice, then rounded out with coconut milk and a sharp squeeze of lime.

ingredients.note: Vegetable stock or water; made up to 1500 ml with boiling water

name: Hazelnut Dacquoise
description: Crisp, cloud-light meringue discs bolstered by toasted hazelnut flour, layered with praline buttercream — crunchy at the edges, chewy at the center, and with a richness that slowly gives way to the clean lift of whipped sugar.

name: Sunflower seed Dacquoise (nut-free)
description: Crisp, cloud-light meringue discs bolstered by ground sunflower seeds, layered with sunflower seed praline buttercream — crunchy at the edges, chewy at the center, and with a richness that slowly gives way to the clean lift of whipped sugar. This nut-free version uses sunflower seeds instead of hazelnuts.

ingredients.note: instead of Hazelnut flour (toasted, skins-on ground hazelnut)
instead of Praline paste (hazelnut, store-bought or home-made)

name: Daifuku Mochi
description: Pillowy rounds of sweet glutinous rice dough — chewy and yielding like nothing else on earth — stretched thin around a generous ball of sweet red bean paste until the filling is completely enveloped and the seam is sealed tight. Dusted in rice flour so the skin stays soft and dry to the touch, each piece is a quiet study in contrasting textures.

ingredients.note: Tsubuan or koshian (sweet red bean paste)

name: Dal Makhani
description: Whole black lentils and kidney beans slow-simmered overnight in tomatoes, butter, and cream — the dal that defines north Indian comfort, rich and midnight-dark.

name: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Thin wheat noodles arrive buried under a thick, sesame-dark sauce that carries the mala numbing heat of Sichuan peppercorn alongside a crispy, caramelized pork mince that is almost more condiment than protein. Each toss of the bowl releases a wave of sesame paste, chili oil, and fermented vegetable brine that smells like a Chengdu street corner at noon.

ingredients.note: Fresh thin wheat noodles (or dried Chinese noodles)
Yibin ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens), rinsed and chopped

name: Dashimaki Tamago
description: A Japanese rolled omelette scented with dashi, sweet with mirin, and built one thin golden layer at a time on a rectangular tamagoyaki pan — silky, spring-loaded, and trembling with custard softness within its spiral cross-section.

name: Dashimaki Tamago (gluten-free)
description: A Japanese rolled omelette scented with dashi, sweet with mirin, and built one thin golden layer at a time on a rectangular tamagoyaki pan — silky, spring-loaded, and trembling with custard softness within its spiral cross-section. This gluten-free version uses tamari (gluten-free soy sauce) instead of soy sauce.

name: Classic Deviled Eggs
description: Hard-boiled eggs halved, yolks beaten with mayonnaise, Dijon, and a touch of vinegar into a tangy, creamy filling piped back into alabaster whites — the party staple that never fails.

ingredients.note: Sweet or smoked paprika, for dusting

name: Doenjang Jjigae
description: Korea's essential soybean-paste stew — doenjang simmered with zucchini, tofu, and mushrooms in a kelp-anchovy broth, intensely savory and deeply comforting in every mouthful.

ingredients.note: Firm or medium tofu, cubed 2 cm
Korean zucchini (or regular zucchini), half-moon sliced

name: Doenjang Jjigae (gluten-free)
description: Korea's essential soybean-paste stew — doenjang simmered with zucchini, tofu, and mushrooms in a kelp-anchovy broth, intensely savory and deeply comforting in every mouthful. This gluten-free version uses white miso paste instead of doenjang (soybean paste).

ingredients.note: Firm or medium tofu, cubed 2 cm
Korean zucchini (or regular zucchini), half-moon sliced

name: Dolmades (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
description: Tender grape leaves rolled around herb-flecked rice with fresh dill and mint, packed tight in a pot and steamed in olive oil and lemon until the leaves turn silky and the filling swells into a compact, fragrant cylinder.

ingredients.note: Grape leaves, preserved in brine (rinsed) or fresh blanched
Extra-virgin olive oil (divided: filling and pot)

name: Dorayaki
description: Two copper-brown, honey-perfumed pancakes sandwiching a thick, yielding layer of anko — sweetened red azuki bean paste. The pancakes are tender and slightly springy from mirin and baking soda, their edges cleanly defined and their surfaces a uniform matte amber.

ingredients.note: Tsubuan or koshian (smooth red bean paste)

name: Dorayaki (gluten-free)
description: Two copper-brown, honey-perfumed pancakes sandwiching a thick, yielding layer of anko — sweetened red azuki bean paste. The pancakes are tender and slightly springy from mirin and baking soda, their edges cleanly defined and their surfaces a uniform matte amber. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.

ingredients.note: instead of Cake flour (or all-purpose + 10% cornstarch)
Tsubuan or koshian (smooth red bean paste)

name: Duck à l'Orange
description: The grand bourgeois roast — a whole duck rendered to crackling, lacquered skin, served beneath a sauce bigarade built on a hair's-breadth caramel gastrique tightened with bitter Seville orange. Sweet, sharp and just shy of burnt, it is the dish that taught a generation what sweet-and-sour could be at the high table.

ingredients.note: Whole duck (2-2.5 kg, trimmed, patted bone-dry)
Seville (bitter) oranges — zest in strips & juice
Brown duck or veal stock (reduced, warm); made up to 900 ml with boiling water
Cold unsalted butter (to mount the sauce)

name: Duck Confit
description: Duck legs cured overnight in coarse salt, herbs, and juniper, then submerged in their own rendered fat and cooked at 90°C until the flesh pulls apart in silken, glossy threads beneath a crackling, copper-brown skin.

ingredients.note: Coarse kosher salt or sel gris
Duck fat (rendered); for frying (only some is absorbed)

name: Chocolate Éclairs
description: The most demanding of the French pastry classics — a hollow shell of pâte à choux that must be absolutely dry and rigid, filled with cold pastry cream that has been folded with whipped cream to silk lightness, sealed with a mirror-gloss dark chocolate fondant that sets in seconds and cracks cleanly when bitten.

name: Chocolate Éclairs (gluten-free)
description: The most demanding of the French pastry classics — a hollow shell of pâte à choux that must be absolutely dry and rigid, filled with cold pastry cream that has been folded with whipped cream to silk lightness, sealed with a mirror-gloss dark chocolate fondant that sets in seconds and cracks cleanly when bitten. This gluten-free version uses gluten-free plain flour blend instead of plain flour.
